overview: The Board granted the Director standing authority to issue early air conditioning variances for multi-unit dwellings during heat waves. Members also reviewed COVID-19 case trends and received comprehensive updates on substance use outreach and climate resiliency programs.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The Board approved the minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: COVID-19 Case Update
items.summary: Director O'Connor reported that weekly cases averaged nearly 300 in May due to a contagious new variant, leading to renewed indoor masking recommendations.

items.title: Vaccination Clinic Logistics
items.summary: The Board discussed transitioning from weekly clinics at City Hall to a regional coordination model with the Mystic Valley Public Health Coalition to improve accessibility.

items.title: Biosafety Permitting Regulations
items.summary: The Director announced that a risk advisor has been retained to review draft biosafety regulations, with a formal consultation scheduled for the June meeting.

items.title: Heat Wave Air Conditioning Variance
items.summary: Approved a motion granting the Director authority to allow multi-unit dwellings to switch from heat to air conditioning before the June 15 state deadline during extreme heat events.

items.title: Office of Prevention and Outreach Update
items.summary: Penny Funaiole detailed the expansion of substance use services, including new recovery coaching roles, grant-funded wraparound supports, and trauma-informed training for court professionals.

items.title: Municipal Vulnerability Preparedness Grant
items.summary: Staff presented progress on climate resiliency initiatives, including the deployment of community liaisons for marginalized populations and plans for local resiliency hubs.

items.title: Combined Sewer Overflow Regulations
items.summary: The Board reviewed new state requirements taking effect in July that mandate public notification within 24 hours of sewage overflows into the river.
